issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a parameterless checkOrderReady() method to be invoked from orderMeal(), but the reference solution implements checkOrderReady with a boolean parameter (checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging)) and calls it with an argument. This deviates from the specified signature and could confuse students about which method signature to implement and how to call it.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the specification by providing a parameterless public void checkOrderReady() method. If logging is desired in the reference solution, add an overloaded private helper (e.g., checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging)) or make the logging optional internally, but keep the public API parameterless so students implement and call checkOrderReady() as described in the problem statement.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void, but the reference implementation defines checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging). This difference in method signature (an extra boolean parameter) breaks the one-to-one mapping between the required API and the solution, and may confuse students about the expected method to implement and call.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the reference implementation with the problem statement by providing a no-argument checkOrderReady() method. Either remove the boolean parameter from the existing method or add an overload public void checkOrderReady() that delegates to checkOrderReady(boolean) internally. Ensure the solution and any example usages call the no-argument variant to match the specification.
